How we rate, in three steps

A fair yardstick

Equity against the style index it tracks most closely; debt against bond funds; hybrid against a matched mix. A small-cap manager has to beat small caps.

Skill, consistency, risk

Alpha and information ratio, how often it was ahead, and how it fell: the measures that lined up best with the next year in our test. Not last year's return.

Reviewed quarterly

Numbers update monthly; ratings every quarter, with a buffer so a strategy does not flip on one month. Large withdrawals count at once.

PMS explained

What a PMS is, who it suits, what it costs and how it is taxed.

₹50 lakhSEBI minimum investment
15–30stocks in a typical PMS strategy
Your nameshares are held in your own demat account
3% / 2% / 1%maximum exit load in years 1, 2 and 3

What PMS is

A portfolio manager registered with SEBI invests on your behalf. Unlike a mutual fund, you own the shares directly, so you see every holding and every trade, and the portfolio can be more concentrated.

Discretionary PMS: the manager decides what to buy and sell. Non-discretionary: the manager advises and acts with your approval. Most investors choose discretionary.

Who it suits

  • Investors who can commit at least ₹50 lakh without needing it for five years or more.
  • Those who already have a core of mutual funds and want a concentrated strategy alongside.
  • People comfortable with returns that can differ sharply from the index, in both directions.

Costs

Fees vary by manager: a fixed fee (often 1.5–2.5% a year), a profit share above a hurdle, or a mix. Performance fees can only be charged on a high-water-mark basis, so you don't pay twice for the same gains. Brokerage, custody and fund-accounting charges come on top.

Costs compound. On ₹50 lakh over 10 years at an assumed 13% a year before fees, a 2.5% yearly fee leaves about ₹19.6 lakh less than a 1% fee would. A PMS has to earn that back to be worth it.

SEBI lets you invest with a portfolio manager directly, without a distributor. Through us, the manager pays us a distribution fee, and we tell you how much before you invest.

Tax

Because the shares are yours, every sale inside the PMS is taxed in your hands: 20% on gains within 12 months, 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh a year after that, plus dividends at your slab. High-turnover strategies therefore cost more in tax than a mutual fund, where trades inside the fund are not taxed until you sell units.

Risks

  • Concentration: 15–30 stocks can fall much more than a diversified fund.
  • Manager risk: results depend on one team; a change of manager can change the strategy.
  • Not guaranteed: PMS returns can be negative, and past returns may not repeat.

How we help

We compare strategies on their reported returns against a standard benchmark (SEBI requires managers to report time-weighted returns against one), their worst periods, fees after tax and how much they overlap with what you already own. We read the disclosure document with you before you sign.

How we work with you

  1. Your goals and current portfolioSo the PMS adds something your mutual funds don't.
  2. A short list of strategiesCompared on record, risk, fees and overlap.
  3. PaperworkAgreement, demat and bank linking with the portfolio manager.
  4. MonitoringQuarterly reports read with you, and a yearly review.

Common questions

What is the minimum investment for PMS?

₹50 lakh, set by SEBI. It can be in cash or in shares you already hold, if the manager accepts them.

Is PMS better than mutual funds?

Not by default. PMS is more concentrated and usually costs more; it is worth it only if the strategy adds return or diversification after those costs.

How is PMS taxed?

Each sale inside the portfolio is taxed in your hands as short- or long-term capital gains, as if you had traded the shares yourself.

Can I exit a PMS early?

Yes. SEBI caps the exit load at 3% in the first year, 2% in the second and 1% in the third; after that, none.

Want a second opinion on a PMS?

Whether you hold one or are considering one, talk to us: we will go through its record, its risks and how it fits with the rest of your money.

Each strategy is compared with its own yardstick: equity with the style index it tracks most closely (total-return), debt with the median high-quality bond mutual fund, hybrid with its fitted mix of the two. Ratings describe past track records and are not a recommendation or a forecast; past performance does not guarantee future returns.
